result.item: FPIA open item D3-b: what to do when a job id/name (that is, a GitHub check-run name) in a complement workflow is the same as the Track C workflow's job 'validate'. Covers AC-32.spoof in track_c_fpia_workflows.py and track_c_fpia_checks.py on Draft PR #42, head 523e702 (head re-checked after a fetch at about 03:25Z). Fix round 3 is uncommitted in wf17/fix3/repo.
result.requirement: A complement workflow (any path of T outside paths(R) ∪ A_V) must not be able to impersonate Track C CI evidence. It must not be accepted as Track C CI evidence, and it must not present itself as the Track C workflow. In return, FPIA must not raise false findings on real owner workflows. Anything it cannot determine must be disclosed and never folded into PASS (CDR-015 unchanged obligations).

alternatives.option: A0: keep what 523e702 and the fix-round-3 draft do. A collision is a note, attached only to a workflow that already has a finding (checks.py L551-563).
alternatives.effect: No false positives. On a clean tree the collision is invisible: the real acaf1b5 run (wf16/v2-real/out/fpia_c1_acaf1b5_A.json) analyses web-mvp-validation.yml and records no collision anywhere.
alternatives.risks: Fails honest reporting, because a real collision is undisclosed. Nothing says how Track C CI evidence must be identified. A byte-identical copy of the Track C workflow at another path is skipped silently (checks.py L520-522; fix3 draft L572-574).

alternatives.option: A1: restore the content-independent rule from dc0bf79 (checks.py L470-471). Any complement job id/name equal to a Track C job id/name is FOUND unless attributed.
alternatives.effect: Measured on 53 trees: the only hit is the Web owner workflow .github/workflows/web-mvp-validation.yml, job 'validate' (5 blobs, on 21 of 39 open PR heads). These include every integration trial: #38 7e3861b, #39 0d31e06, #40 acaf1b5, #42 523e702, plus #31 and #35. That workflow cannot be attributed under the F5 rule, so every realistic Track C + Web candidate gives FPIA_FAIL.
alternatives.risks: A 100% false-positive rate on current integration trees, which is the reason F5 removed this rule. Clearing it needs a change to another owner's CI. It is also unsound without constant folding: `name: ${{ matrix.n }}` or `format()` can produce 'validate'.

alternatives.option: A2: A1 plus an allowlist of known owner workflows (web-mvp-validation.yml).
alternatives.effect: Removes the measured false positive.
alternatives.risks: A path-specific exception, which earlier rounds ruled out. It must be maintained for every new owner workflow, and it adds no protection: matching of a check-run name is still name-only on GitHub's side.

alternatives.option: A3 (recommended): a generic collision stays non-blocking but is always detected and disclosed. Track C CI evidence is identified by workflow-run path + head_sha + authenticated workflow blob, never by check-run name. A job id, job name or check-run name containing the Track C workflow identity key is FOUND. The exemption for byte-identical copies at another path is removed. A re-decision trigger is set for required checks.
alternatives.effect: No new verdicts on any measured tree: 0 FOUND from the new rules across 53 trees. The web-mvp-validation collision becomes visible in every output. The identity actually used as evidence (run path, which GitHub cannot let a different file share) is written into the contract.
alternatives.risks: A complement job named 'validate' still produces a check run that has the same name as Track C's. This is disclosed, not prevented. If someone later adds a required status check on 'validate' without re-deciding, impersonation becomes live (hence the trigger).

alternatives.option: A4: route to the Track C owner a successor Track C workflow with a unique job name (for example `name: track-c-evl-validation`).
alternatives.effect: Removes the ambiguity at the source.
alternatives.risks: Changes Track C CI identity (INFRA_REPLACE projection path, needs a new CDR manifest R). It belongs to another owner (single-writer rule). Not needed while no required checks exist. Keep it as the recovery path.

alternatives.option: A5: route the Web owner to rename job 'validate' in web-mvp-validation.yml.
alternatives.effect: Removes today's only collision.
alternatives.risks: Rewrites another owner's CI identity and changes 5 blob lineages across 21 PR heads. It does not prevent future collisions. Keep it as recovery only.

alternatives.option: A6: add branch protection or rulesets with required checks keyed on Track C check names.
alternatives.effect: Would automate a merge gate.
alternatives.risks: Makes the collision exploitable: GitHub matches a required check by check-run name plus app, and every workflow here shares app github-actions (id 15368). Do not adopt without A1 or A4 first.

result.decision:
Adopt A3 as a PIW self-decision under CDR-015 and record it as the next entry in PIW_DECISION_RECORDS.md:
(1) A job id/name or check-run name equal to a Track C job id or check-run name ('validate') does not by itself make AC-32.spoof FOUND and does not change any verdict.
(2) FPIA computes the effective GitHub check-run name of every job in every analysed complement workflow. It always lists collisions (comparison: H1 identity-key equality) and the names it cannot determine, whether or not the workflow has a finding.
(3) A job id, job name or effective check-run name whose H1 identity key contains the Track C workflow name/stem key 'trackcevlvalidation' is FOUND. This extends the H1 workflow-identity claim to jobs; it is specific, not generic.
(4) A complement file byte-identical to the authenticated Track C workflow is no longer exempt. Such a file is always a copy at another path, because the real path is in paths(R) and therefore never in the complement. It is FOUND as an identity claim.
(5) Contract rule: Track C CI evidence is identified only by:
- workflow-run path == .github/workflows/track-c-evl-validation.yml,
- head_sha of the audited or recorded commit,
- the Track C workflow blob at that head_sha belonging to the authenticated R/V blobs,
- and the run and job ids.
It is never identified by check-run name, job id or workflow display name. FPIA itself verifies no GitHub check run, and says so.
(6) Precondition and trigger: the repository has no branch protection, rulesets or required status checks (measured 2026-10-05 ~03:20Z). If one is introduced that references a Track C check-run name, or any consumer accepts Track C CI by check name, a superseding decision (A1 together with A4 or A5) is needed before it is relied on.
Sequencing: apply this after fix round 3 commits (a follow-up commit on the PIW-owned integration/fpia-hardened-v1), so the running fix round is not disturbed.
result.classification:
D2. This is a policy choice and an acceptance-contract change (FPIA AC-32.spoof semantics plus the rule for identifying evidence) needed for the project goal. CDR-015 lists FPIA D3-a…e explicitly as D2.
- Not D3-cost: no paid resource. The repo is public, the change adds no runner usage, and the measurement used read-only API calls.
- Not outside the delegation: no orders, no fund movements, nothing outside the project.
- It does not authorise changing repository settings or other owners' workflows: A4 and A5 are routed, and A6 is not adopted.
result.reason:
The requirement is about evidence identity, so it is enforced where identity is decided, not through a generic word.
1. GitHub names a job's check run with the job name (or id) only, and all Actions check runs here share app github-actions id 15368. Measured: on acaf1b5, check run 111368102118 'validate' belongs to run 37179194376 (web-mvp-validation, path .github/workflows/web-mvp-validation.yml, workflow_id 369058605). On b9e01a9, check run 111129291040 'validate' belongs to run 37097149378 (track-c-evl-validation, path .github/workflows/track-c-evl-validation.yml, workflow_id 369044666). On 523e702, six different workflows each produce a check run named 'offline'. A check-run name therefore cannot identify Track C evidence; the run path can, because two files cannot share a path. The content of the Track C path itself is already protected by the projection (INFRA_REPLACE).
2. Nothing in the repository consumes check runs by name. There is no branch protection, ruleset or required check, and no code on any branch or PR head uses check-run names. The project already cites Track C CI by run id + workflow file + event + head_sha (GIE-009, GLOBAL_HANDOFF_HISTORY L59). A content-independent rule would block no live attack.
3. The one real collision is a legitimate owner workflow present in every integration trial. A1 fails all of them (the reason F5 was introduced in 465354a), and A2 brings back path-specific exceptions.
4. The status quo hides the collision on clean trees and exempts copies of the Track C workflow, which conflicts with honest reporting. A3 fixes both at measured false-positive cost 0.
5. The specific identity key 'trackcevlvalidation' on job names had 0 hits in 53 trees, so FOUND costs nothing. A substring rule on the generic word 'validate' would only add noise, because GitHub's own matching is exact.

result.requirement:
An FPIA verdict used to accept a canonical or integration merge must come from an FPIA version that the audited change T cannot alter. That breaks down into five parts. (1) The verifier's identity, meaning every file it loads, is fixed by an authenticated record that T does not control. (2) The execution channel, meaning the command or workflow definition, is not taken from T. (3) The verdict on T does not exempt or trust any of T's own content because it looks like the verifier. (4) Changes to FPIA itself are audited by the previously authenticated verifier, and the new code's own self-audit is reported separately. (5) Integrity digests are not presented as authentication. CDR-015 also requires that unverified scope is disclosed and never folded into PASS, and that records stay append-only.

Today none of this holds:
- On pull_request, `track-c-fpia.yml` checks out the PR head and runs `python implementation/tools/integration/track_c_fpia.py` from that checkout. The workflow definition also comes from the PR merge ref.
- All 3 FPIA CI runs were self-audits: 37214415914 (T=465354a), 37230761722 (T=babf0a4) and 37234682864 (T=523e702).
- `runtime_provenance.verifier` covers 9 of the 29 verifier-set files at 523e702. It omits the 19 `_vendor` files and the workflow, and it is self-reported.
- The `fpia-output: VERIFIED` line in CI is printed by the same code that wrote the output.
- FPIA classifies its own paths as complement by design (`test_integration_fpia_self.py::test_fpia_files_complement_clean`), so no verifier version flags a T that rewrites FPIA.

alternatives.option: A0 Status quo: PR CI runs T's own FPIA; runtime_provenance.verifier records commit and blobs only
alternatives.effect: No change. The PR CI gives a fast signal.
alternatives.risks: Every PR that edits FPIA or the workflow certifies itself (3 of 3 runs so far are self-audits). After merge, any later edit silently changes every future verdict. Provenance covers 9 of 29 files and is self-reported, so a malicious verifier can print anything. The CI log anchor for --expect-result-sha256 is also printed by T-controlled code. Violates the requirement.

alternatives.option: A1 Run the PR base branch's FPIA copy against T
alternatives.effect: Needs no new authority record.
alternatives.risks: The base is just another branch anyone with push access can move; it is not authenticated. PR #42's base acaf1b5 has no FPIA, so its own CI would be NOT_RUN. Stacked integration bases change often. The workflow definition is still taken from the PR merge ref, so T can drop the base-copy step. Rejected as the authority.

alternatives.option: A2 pull_request_target (workflow taken from the default branch)
alternatives.effect: The workflow definition is out of T's reach.
alternatives.risks: Since 2025-12-08 pull_request_target always uses the default branch, here canonical claude/investment-system-top500-validation-alrugm @ b8e39a2, which has no FPIA. It is unusable until a canonical merge. On public repositories (this repo is public) GitHub will disable it by default from 2026-11-02 unless an Actions policy allows it (secondary source; see unverified). It runs T's full regression in a privileged context (secrets, token), the classic 'pwn request' pattern. Rejected now.

alternatives.option: A3 Workflow defined on integration/global-handoff-v1, run by workflow_dispatch with ref=handoff or by push
alternatives.effect: The definition comes from the PIW single-writer authority branch.
alternatives.risks: The dispatch-only FPIA workflow returned 404 in the dc0bf79 round (not on the default branch, not registered). A push trigger would put CI on the authority branch and run on every handoff append. The result is not attached to the PR. Deferred.

alternatives.option: A4 Fail closed (NOT_RUN) whenever T changes any verifier path
alternatives.effect: Simple and safe for verifier changes.
alternatives.risks: FPIA fixes could never be integrated. 1. **Pin authority.** The PIW appends to `implementation/docs/coordination/PIW_DECISION_RECORDS.md` on integration/global-handoff-v1 (0 entries today) a PDR with a fenced `fpia-verifier-pin` JSON block. The block holds:
   - `pin_id` and `pdr`;
   - `commit` P;
   - `manifest`: path to blob for every file under `implementation/tools/integration/`, excluding `__pycache__`, *.pyc and *.pyo. That is 28 paths at 523e702: 9 track_c_fpia*.py and 19 `_vendor` files.
   - `manifest_sha256`;
   - `ci_workflow`: `{path: .github/workflows/track-c-fpia.yml, blob}`;
   - `supersedes` (the previous pin_id, or null);
   - `revokes`;
   - `evidence` (GIE ids).

   FPIA reads the pin at the register commit G under the CDR-014 rules: G is an ancestor of the authority tip read by ls-remote, and the file at G is a byte prefix of the file at the tip. Exactly one chain is valid; the last non-revoked block is current.

2. **Acceptance-grade verdict.** Only a result with all of the following counts:
   - `verifier_authentication = PINNED_AUTHENTICATED`, meaning the running verifier's git manifest equals the pin manifest, the worktree is clean (including `_vendor`), and P is reachable from the authority remote;
   - `fpia.status = FPIA_PASS`;
   - produced by the PIW from a clean worktree at P (`git worktree add --detach <dir> P`) against T, with `--register-commit G`.

   - When CI's workflow blob, at `merge-tree(base, head)`, equals the pinned `ci_workflow` blob, its `verdict_sha256` must equal the local one. Any disagreement makes the result NOT_ELIGIBLE until it is explained.
   - When the CI channel is T_DEFINED or the run is missing, this is recorded and disclosed. It does not block acceptance, but it is never counted as corroboration.

3. **Self-placement exemptions.** The fix-round-3 `VerifierSelf` rule must exempt only files whose path and blob equal the authenticated pin manifest, plus earlier pins only if the pin block lists them. result.requirement:
1) CDR-015 (2026-10-05 12:15 KST): scope we did not detect or verify must be disclosed and never folded into an overall PASS. Failures are never hidden. PIT, provenance and evidence integrity, and honest reporting all stay in force. Every self-decision records reason, impact, verification and recovery, in PIW_DECISION_RECORDS.md.
2) CDR-014 §5/§7/§10: FPIA must prove that the Track C projection is preserved and free of interference, and must fail closed where provenance cannot be verified. The statuses FPIA_PASS/FAIL/NOT_RUN and INTEGRATION_INTERFERENCE_NONE/FOUND must be kept. §15 adds no new numeric threshold.
3) The facts behind D3-c:
 (a) Complement CI workflows are never executed by FPIA. AC-32.spoof is static only.
 (b) FPIA's T-full lane does run complement tests. But a complement importer of Track C is detected only statically: AC-21 uses fd.module_imports, which accepts only constant import_module/__import__/run_module. check_trace(track_c=False) does not attribute Track C imports to the frames that caused them.
 (c) Complete static detection of computed targets is undecidable.
4) What the requirement therefore demands: a precisely bounded non-claim that is always visible, plus every cheap mitigation that does not create false findings on legitimate trees.

Adopt B + E as PIW decision record PDR-D3C, under CDR-015 D2.
(1) NC-D3C becomes a decided, bounded non-claim. It is no longer an 'open user decision'.
(2) FPIA_PASS keeps its token and exit code 0, but is always reported as SCOPE_QUALIFIED. The non-claims in force appear in result.scope (covered by result_sha256), in the summary line for every status, and in the CI step summary as annotations. GIE, merge and handoff records must quote the qualifier.
(3) M1 stays as landed at 11d2f25. Literal mentions of M in complement workflows and every in-tree code file they reach are FOUND.
(4) Add M2. Fold constant-only Python string expressions: + concatenation, f-strings with only constant fields, str.join/format/% over constants, slicing including [::-1], replace/lower/upper/strip, os.path/posixpath.join, pathlib '/' of constants, base64/bytes.fromhex decoding of literals. Also substitute literal shell assignments (NAME=literal, export) and literal YAML env values into $NAME/${NAME}. Run mention matching and fd.module_imports (AC-21) over the folded values. Folding only adds findings; it never removes one.
(5) Add M3, in the T-full lane only. The child wraps builtins.__import__, importlib.import_module, importlib.util.spec_from_file_location and runpy.run_path/run_module, reusing the existing spawn audit events. A Track C module or file requested by a complement frame becomes finding AC-21.runtime. This is the same L3 policy as the static importer rule. Attribution exceptions are unchanged.
(6) Everything outside these layers stays NOT_CLAIMED. That is: targets that depend on run-time input, and lookups that bypass the import system.
(7) Ship as small verified bundles on integration/fpia-hardened-v1, after 11d2f25, as a single writer and without rewriting fix round 3:
 - bundle 1: wording, scope fields, summary, CI and schema TRACK_C_FPIA/3 (D1);
 - bundle 2: M2;
 - bundle 3: M3.
(8) Do not adopt C, D or F.
result.classification: D2 under CDR-015. It is a policy choice about what FPIA certifies and what an FPIA_PASS means for integration acceptance. It is also a contract change to the FPIA output (schema /3), and M3 can change verification results. The PIW decides and executes it with evidence; no user re-approval is needed. The implementation pieces (wording, summary, M2, tests) are D1. It is not D3: everything uses local compute or the existing public-repo CI, and no paid resource or quota is involved. It is not outside the delegation: there are no securities orders, no fund movements and no external actions; alternative D is rejected partly because workflow steps call external services.
result.reason:
1) Completeness is impossible: a target can be built from run-time input such as env, files, enumeration or network. So the only honest resolution is a bound that is stated exactly, with the verdict qualified by it (B). That is what CDR-015 asks for.
2) Fail-closed heuristics (C) are measured to flip the legitimate subject acaf1b5 (6 of 14 workflows) and 7 of 16 complement workflow paths across all PR heads, and they would still be incomplete.
3) Executing the workflows (D) is infeasible and causes external side effects.
4) M2 and M3 shrink the residual at measured zero false-positive cost:
 - M2: 0 new hits across 45 trees.
 - M3: 0 events across the 1517 tests at acaf1b5.
 Together they turn the residual into a semantic class ('the target depends on run-time input, or the access bypasses the import system') rather than a syntactic accident.
5) The harm of the residual is bounded by controls that do not depend on D3-c:
 - H1 identity keys fail closed on any Track C-looking or non-foldable workflow name, so a dynamic invocation cannot run under the Track C identity.
 - Projection byte identity (AC-15..21) means Track C code and evidence in T cannot be altered.
 - FPIA never relies on complement CI output. It replays the Frozen tools itself in hardened lanes.
 - AC-35 catches cross-test interference with Track C test outcomes in the shared session.
 So a missed dynamic invocation can only produce output attributed to a non-Track C workflow or test. It cannot change Track C bytes or the FPIA evidence.

4) GIE-014 and later records, the PR #42 body, and GLOBAL_CURRENT_HANDOFF line 80 (which today reads 'Open decisions … (not decided): … D3-c') must use the scope-qualified wording.
5) The T-full lane gets roughly 6% slower, measured once under uncontrolled load. The CI timeout of 150 minutes is unaffected.
6) No owner branch, Frozen record or Track C file is touched.
7) Still not claimed:
 - invocations whose target depends on run-time input (environment, repository variables or secrets, workflow inputs or event data, data files read at run time, directory enumeration, command output, network);
 - sys.modules lookups and attribute access on packages that are already imported;
 - code paths the suite does not execute;
 - grandchild processes whose argv does not name Track C;

result.recovery:
1) Wording, summary and schema changes: revert the bundle-1 commit, or supersede it with a later PDR entry. No history rewrite or force-push. /2 and /3 outputs stay distinguishable by schema and verifier commit.
2) M2 or M3 producing a finding on a legitimate tree: report the finding as it is, never suppressed. The PIW then records a superseding PDR that either attributes the caller through the normal owner-evidence channel, or narrows the rule with a recorded reason and a regression test. Reverting the M2 or M3 commit restores 11d2f25 behaviour; NC-D3C must then be widened again in the same commit, to include constant-built targets (M2) or computed imports in the T-full session (M3).
3) If the residual is later judged unacceptable, for example after an incident, a successor PDR can require instrumented execution of complement workflows on runners. That must first establish cost: free on this public repository for standard runners; any paid runner or exceeded quota is D3.
4) Irreversible: none. Past evidence and records are untouched.

"NC-D3C (PIW decision PDR-D3C under CDR-015 D2): FPIA does not claim to detect an invocation of Track C code, tests or modules by a complement workflow or complement code when the invoked target is constructed from run-time input. Run-time input means: environment, repository variables or secrets, workflow inputs or event data, files read at run time (data, not code), directory enumeration, command output, network or API responses, or a computed import name that does not reduce to constants. Detected, and FOUND unless attributed:
- literal mentions of the authenticated Track C mention set M and of Track C paths in complement workflows and every in-tree code file they reach, after YAML decoding, GitHub constant-expression folding and Python/shell constant folding;
- static and constant-folded imports of Track C modules (AC-21);
- for code executed by FPIA's own full-regression session, every import, load or launch request for a Track C module or file made by complement code (AC-21.runtime).
Not detected: access that bypasses the import system (sys.modules lookups, attribute access on already-imported packages), code paths the session does not execute, and grandchild processes whose argv does not name Track C. Complement workflows are never executed by FPIA. FPIA_PASS is therefore SCOPE_QUALIFIED. It does not state that no complement code invokes Track C."

result.decision:
Adopt C as PIW decision G7-1 under CDR-015.

1. Scope. Every canonical merge-result SHA, and every integration merge result the PIW presents as a landing candidate or vehicle, gets an FPIA record on that exact SHA. FPIA first decides applicability, using the authenticated R and V from the CDR-014 manifest.

2. APPLICABLE when any of these holds:
- R is an ancestor of T;
- T has at least one Track C-namespace path (Projection.ns derived from R's frozen tools);
- T has .github/workflows/track-c-evl-validation.yml;
- T has any path matching implementation/tools/track_c_*acceptance*.py;
- T has any A_V-type path.
When applicable, the full FPIA is mandatory and only FPIA_PASS admits the landing (CDR-014 unchanged). FAIL and NOT_RUN block it.

3. NOT_APPLICABLE (FPIA_NOT_APPLICABLE, exit 3) only when all of these hold:
- caller repository and environment PASS (non-shallow, no fetch problems);
- authority PASS;
- derivation succeeded;
- every T-independent reference check passes (V descends from R; anchors and Frozen evidence heads are ancestors of R; approvals consistent; no unbound evidence);
- R is not an ancestor of T and none of the markers in item 2 is present.
Anything else gives NOT_RUN or FAIL, never NOT_APPLICABLE.
- The AC-04 entry for this case is kept verbatim with status NOT_APPLICABLE.
- The other two AC-04 cases (NON_MERGE_PRESERVING_LANDING, broadened to cover a stale Track C head; and R_ABSENT_TRACK_C_NAMESPACE_PATHS_PRESENT) stay FAIL.
- NOT_APPLICABLE is never PASS, never Track C acceptance, and never counts toward Track C INTEGRATED. The landing then rests on the bundle's own capability evidence.

4. One-way rule. After the first canonical SHA that contains R, every later canonical SHA is APPLICABLE by construction:
- R's ancestry cannot be removed without a history rewrite, which is forbidden;
- a revert keeps R and then fails the projection check.
Every canonical advance is therefore audited before landing and after:
- Before: the PIW builds M with `git merge --no-ff` on the current canonical tip, audits M, fast-forwards canonical to exactly M, and verifies that the remote equals M. No squash, rebase or merge button for applicable merges.
- After: a push audit on the default branch, once track-c-fpia.yml is on canonical.

5. The Track C landing is the first APPLICABLE canonical SHA. Its complement includes everything landed before it, so latent problems surface there (for example #28's importer gives AC-21 FAIL).

6. NOT_APPLICABLE records list latent Track C references in T (Python importers of Track C modules). A pre-Track-C bundle with a non-empty list is not landed until its resolution is recorded. Today that is only #28 (1 file); its D3-d decision covers it.

7. CI:
- Triggers: pull_request where the base is the default branch or the base or head is integration/*; push to the default branch; workflow_dispatch.
- Job 1, fpia-applicability: determines applicability and fails only on FAIL or NOT_RUN.
- Job 2, fpia: needs job 1 and runs only when APPLICABLE (always on dispatch). A NOT_APPLICABLE tree shows the audit job as skipped, never green.
- Subject: the PR head when the base tip is its ancestor (fast-forward landing SHA). Otherwise the GitHub test merge, labelled MERGE_PREVIEW and never landing evidence.

8. Classification and limits. This decision is D2 and executes only on the PIW-owned Draft PR #42 branch, after fix round 3 has landed (no concurrent writer). It merges nothing. Any canonical merge, including landing track-c-fpia.yml, stays under CDR-016's narrower rule in this Work: explicit user approval naming it.
